title: A7 exclusion race: sweep_terminal lacks the taken_over_at guard this PR added to every sibling sweep step — a take-over mid-tick terminalizes a landlord-handled row, killing the §8.6 late-completion form link
evidence:
sweep_terminal.sql:30-32: 'WHERE id = $1
  AND status = 'contact_initiated'
  AND attempt_count = 4' — no taken_over_at filter. Contrast the same PR's r1 N12 guards: sweep_claim_t0.sql:34 'AND taken_over_at IS NULL' and sweep_advance.sql:25 'AND taken_over_at IS NULL'. The only exclusion is the due-SELECT (sweep_due_reference_calls.sql:59 'AND rc.taken_over_at IS NULL'), a snapshot taken at tick start: a take-over landing between the SELECT and the T+144h UPDATE still commits, terminalizing the taken-over row to unreachable/partial (form link dies, §8.6 broken).
detail: r1 N12 guarded claim_t0 + advance but missed the T+144h terminal writer; step_terminal (sweep.gleam:540) has no re-check. Taken-over row at attempt_count=4 is terminalized despite the landlord's A7 marker.
recommended_fix: Add 'AND taken_over_at IS NULL' to sweep_terminal.sql's WHERE (mirroring sweep_claim_t0/sweep_advance); a 0-row stand-down is already handled. Pin with a race-style test if feasible.

title: Wrong-person first-failure leg is only Gleam-guarded against take-over: update_reference_call_status has no taken_over_at backstop, so the r2-BLOCKER scenario survives as a TOCTOU on the wrong-person route
evidence:
form_handler.gleam:1235: 'case row.taken_over_at != "" { True -> wisp.redirect(to: "/reference/" <> token)' — the check reads the row from lookup_context; the write leg then runs sql/update_reference_call_status (form_handler.gleam:1267-1274), whose guard is update_reference_call_status.sql:23-24: 'WHERE id = $1
  AND status = $5::reference_call_status' — no taken_over_at filter. Contrast the webhook leg's mark_awaiting_correction.sql:23 'AND taken_over_at IS NULL'. A take-over committing between the read and the UPDATE still yanks the landlord-handled row to awaiting_correction.
detail: Narrow race (sub-ms between lookup and UPDATE), no fraud fabrication, but the wrong-person leg of the r2 BLOCKER has no SQL-side stand-down — the fix is read-side only, unlike the webhook legs.
recommended_fix: Route the wrong-person awaiting_correction write through a taken_over_at-guarded UPDATE (or add the filter to a dedicated query for this leg), matching mark_awaiting_correction.sql's guard.
